newsitem.title: UK: IPE June Brent sheds some losses despite U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: IPE June Brent sheds some losses despite U.S. data.

text.p: IPE Brent futures shed some of their earlier losses on Wednesday after NYMEX opened weeker following more bearish weekly U.S. stock figures, but soon recovered to trade a little stronger than expected, traders said.

June Brent was trading 37 cents down at $19.25 a barerl by 1348 GMT, right after NYMEX's WTI June contract opened some 47 cents weaker at $20.90, in line with their opening call. But within 20 to 30 minutes, June Brent was at $19.37 while WTI was at $21.03.
"I am really baffled by those figures -- look at the WTI at $20.10 now," one IPE trader said.
"Based on the API (American Petroleum Institute) data, the market here should be sold, that's what I am telling my clients, and it should be heading down, but look at it, it is heading up."

Another London trader said: "The market has been New York-led. London did not think much of the APIs, did not like them at all and we came off, but New York looks like they've decided to regard them as extremely suspect. So the market has reacted a little positively here."

June Brent lost in earlier trade on the back of the bearish API stock data, released late on Tuesday, which showed that crude stocks in the United States rose 6.94 million barrels to 322.63 million in the May 9 week.
According to the API, gasoline stocks grew to 197.06 million barrels in the week ending May 9 -- a rise of 6.51 million barrels.
Weekly data released on Wednesday by the U.S. Department of Energy were largely in line with the APIs.

The Energy Information Administration (EIA) said U.S. crude stocks rose by 6.4 million barrels to 323.7 million barrels while gasoline stocks were up 4.7 million barrels over the same period at 198.3 million.
The EIA figures showed a distillates draw of 400,000 barrels to 96.4 million barrels.
Gas oil also shed some of its earlier losses when it fell as low as $169.75 right before NYMEX opened, and it was trading $2.50 a tonne down at $170.75 by 1421 GMT.
